:::{#def-ratio}
#### Ratios

A **ratio** is a quotient in which the numerator and denominator are measured using the same unit scales.

::: notes
cf. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio>
:::

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-ratio}
#### A ratio, and a quotient that is not one

- A board $150$ cm long and one $75$ cm long have length ratio
  $\tfrac{150 \text{ cm}}{75 \text{ cm}} = 2$:
  both lengths are in centimeters, so the units cancel and the ratio has none.
- $12$ cases in $4$ weeks gives the quotient
  $\tfrac{12 \text{ cases}}{4 \text{ weeks}} = 3$ cases per week.
  The numerator and denominator are in different units,
  so this quotient is not a ratio; it is a rate (@def-rate).

:::
